metadata.note: Modern-day Amtrak intercity rail network, as of the GTFS feed pulled from https://content.amtrak.com/content/gtfs/GTFS.zip. Route geometry is real, sourced directly from Amtrak's own published shapes (Douglas-Peucker simplified to ~300m tolerance to keep file size reasonable). Frequency (headway_min) is REAL, computed from actual scheduled trip counts on a representative Wednesday (2026-08-19-ish service pattern) in this feed — not an estimate, unlike the historical-era files in this dataset. Each route is represented as a single-year segment (2026) since GTFS has no historical depth; it does not claim the route or its frequency existed at any other year. Only Amtrak-branded (agency_id 51) rail routes are included — Amtrak Thruway connecting buses, Via Rail Canada's joint Maple Leaf listing, and commuter services that share Amtrak's feed (MARC, Shore Line East) are excluded. Each route also carries avg_speed_kmh, computed from real scheduled trip duration (stop_times.txt) divided by route length — used so faster corridors animate faster and don't show an inflated number of simultaneous trains. CORRECTION (2026-08-18): the Acela and Northeast Regional features originally used each route's single most-frequent GTFS shape, which for both is a New York-Washington-only variant, so the entire New York-New Haven-Providence-Boston half of the Northeast Corridor was missing. Both now use the full Boston-Washington shapes (Acela 327, Northeast Regional 264) from the same feed, with avg_speed_kmh recomputed from stop_times over the corrected route length. CORRECTION (2026-08-24): the Lake Shore Limited had the same single-most-frequent-shape problem as Acela and Northeast Regional. Its representative shape was 125, the Boston section, so in New York State the train was drawn arriving from Massachusetts with its whole New York Penn - Albany run down the Hudson Line missing -- which is why it looked nothing like the Maple Leaf south of Albany, even though the two are vertex-for-vertex identical on the track they really share (Rensselaer to Buffalo: 75 identical vertices, median separation 0.000 km). amtrak-81 now uses shape 128, the New York section, and the Boston section is a separate feature (amtrak-81-boston) drawn only Boston - Rensselaer so the shared trunk is not double-drawn. The same pass found Empire Service drawn as New York - Albany-Rensselaer only (shape 245); its four daily Niagara Falls trains are now drawn as amtrak-36921-west from shape 279. These four features come from a fresh GTFS pull dated 20260824; the rest of the file is still the 20260816 pull. Where the Maple Leaf and Lake Shore diverge west of Buffalo -- Maple Leaf north to Niagara Falls and Toronto, Lake Shore southwest along Lake Erie toward Erie, PA -- that is real and was left alone. CORRECTION (2026-08-24, same day): the Empire Service western feature added earlier that day was drawn Albany-Rensselaer to Niagara Falls from 1971. That was wrong at the Niagara Falls end -- the city had no passenger service between 1961 and the opening of its Amtrak station on October 29 1978. The feature now ends at Buffalo, and the Buffalo - Niagara Falls tail is amtrak-36921-niagara, starting 1978.
metadata.line_label_audit: 2026-08-24: line labels normalised repo-wide to "<operating company>: <line name>" -- the company's common display name (legal suffixes dropped), then the line as a passenger would have known it, or its two terminals where the line carried no advertised name. Long intermediate station lists were reduced to endpoints. For features spanning several operators the company shown is the one that ran the line for most of its drawn years. See CLAUDE.md Rule 6.
metadata.branch_geometry_fill: 2026-08-30: added 7 feature(s) for track no Amtrak feature drew, found by comparing every GTFS shape against the whole drawn network rather than against each route's own feature. Most apparent gaps were not gaps -- the Texas Eagle west of San Antonio runs on the Sunset Limited's rails, the Pacific Surfliner north of Los Angeles on the Coast Starlight's, the Springfield Line on the Hartford Line's -- and drawing those would have stacked a duplicate line on identical track. Branch start years are sourced individually where known and inherited from the parent feature, marked NOT SOURCED FOR THIS BRANCH, where not.
